texts.preamble: Natwar Singh @ Satyam Singh vs State Of U.P. on 7 November, 2019 Author: Manju Rani Chauhan Bench: Manju Rani Chauhan High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 78 Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 47693 of 2019 Applicant :- Natwar Singh @ Satyam Singh
texts.facts: The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-Natwar Singh @ Satyam Singh with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No. 273 of 2018, under Sections 419, 420, 272, 273 I.P.C. and Sections 60, 63 and 72 of Excise Act, Police Station-Rasra, District-Ballia, during the pendency of the trial. As per the version of the first information report, on raid by the Police party on 25th September, 2019, it was found that six-seven persons including the applicant were loading contraband adulterated liquors in a tractor trolley. Except the co-accused, Anil Singh, the other co-accused persons ran away. Total 4850 bottles of 180 ml. each contraband adulterated liquors was alleged to Natwar Singh @ Satyam Singh vs State Of U.P. on 7 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114144905/ 1 have been recovered.
texts.arguments: It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with some ulterior motive. Neither anything incriminating material has been recovered from the possession of the applicant nor he has been arrested from the spot. It is further submitted that Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been enacted by the legislature and hence the implication of the applicant under section 272, 273, I.P.C. is unjustified. Offence under sections 60,63, 72 of Excise Act is bailable and trible by Magistrate. False recovery has been alleged. Apart from the above, it is also submitted that the co-accused, namely, Anil Singh, Ankit Singh and Durgesh Singh have already been enlarged on bail by the Coordinate Benches of this Court, copies of their bail orders have been enclosed as Annexure-3 to the affidavit accompanying the present bail application. The case of the applicant is similar and identical to that of the aforesaid co-accused. As such, the applicant is also liable to be enlarged on bail. The applicant has no criminal history. It is next contended that there is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the witnesses and in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail. The applicant is in jail since 14th October, 2019. Per contra learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant but he could not dispute the factual submissions as urged by the learned counsel for the applicant.
